newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - Advanced Aero jumps.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - Advanced Aero jumps.

text.p: Advanced Aerodynamics & Structures Inc units jumped 55 percent at the company's market debut after its initial public offering on Tuesday.

The units added 2-5/8 to 7-5/8 in early trading as investors snapped up shares of the Long Beach, California development-stage company, which designs and manufactures propjet and jet aircraft primarily for business use.
Advanced Aerodynamics offered six million units which priced at $5 each. DH Blair Investment Banking Corp is the lead underwriter of the offering.
Other companies that made their IPO debuts on Tuesday:

-- ViaSat Inc shares inched up 1/2 to 9-1/2. It priced 2.2 million shares below its estimated range of $10 - $12. The Carlsbad, California company filed in October for the offering with Oppenheimer & Co as its lead underwriter.

Of the total number of shares, the company offered 1.65 million while selling shareholders offered 550,000. Viasat designs, produces and markets advanced digital satellite telecommunications and wireless signal processing equipment.
It posted a profit of $1.3 million in 1995 on revenues of $22.3 million, according to a regulatory filing.

-- Shares of U.S. Energy Systems Inc were trading flat at $4 each. The West Palm Beach, Florida company offered 3.1 million shares and redeemable warrants with shares pricing at $4 each and warrants for $0.10 each. It develops and operates independent power plants. Gaines Berland was the lead underwriter of the offering.
-- Shares of Translation Group Ltd were priced at $6 each but had not yet begun trading near midday. The Pennsauken, New Jersey company translates documents and software.
